Subject: Interop & observability: next technical tests and validation steps

Hi Evelyn & team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about NimbleHealth's latency targets and the telemetry you need for compliance. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single place to track actions.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary goal: ensure realtime inference at 50–75ms p50 for 1k qps bursts, and full auditability for every request (trace id + token accounting).
- You're running a mix of synchronous API calls (customer-facing chat) and batch scoring (nightly pipeline) — both important for cost/SLAs.
- Primary hyperscaler concerns: managed endpoint cold-starts, telemetry sampling gaps, and lack of per-request token breakdowns.

Where Redwood stands (high level):
- Differentiators you asked about: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private; automatic KV cache to reduce tail latency; token-level cost telemetry exposed per-request.
- Hyperscaler delta: we can provide predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated) and built-in prefix caching; hyperscalers rely on instance autoscale which caused variability in our customers' tests.

Proposed next technical tests (we'll own setup for the Redwood side):
1) Observability parity test: run a 30-minute 500 qps steady-state + 10k qps burst window, validate per-request traces, token counts, and latency SLOs. (Deliverable: obs logs + trace samples)
2) Cold-start/scale test: toggle capacity down to 0 and send sudden 5k qps ramp to measure tail behavior and fallback policies.
3) Model variant fallback: verify graceful degrade from large model -> quantized variant without request failures.
4) Cost accounting comparison: run identical prompt set against Redwood Dedicated vs your current hyperscaler endpoint and compare per-token cost and end-to-end latency.

Ask from you:
- Confirm priority of tests (1–4 above).
- Provide a contact for infra to coordinate IPs / allowlist and a preferred window for the lab run (we suggest Wed/Thu next week).
- Any PII safe examples for a small prompt set (or we can use synthetic prompts).

I've attached a short test protocol and a preliminary comparison sheet (spreadsheet). I'll open a HubSpot task and a Drive folder we can both use.

Attachments: 20260711-redwood-hyperscaler-comparison.xlsx, obs-test-protocol-v1.pdf

Thanks — I'll wait for the priorities and infra contact and we'll schedule a tech deep-dive.

Best,

Jasmine — good summary. A few technical notes / suggested additions before we hand this to the lab team: 

1) Observability parity test: include a synthetic tracing header to assert end-to-end trace id propagation through any proxies. Also capture KV cache hit/miss rates and per-request memory usage for long-context sessions.

2) Sampling: we should disable sampling for the duration of the test (sample=100%) so Nimble can see full token-level breakdowns; after that we can show how sampling reduces telemetry volume with minimal loss.

3) Metrics to collect (minimum): request_id, trace_id, model_variant, tokens_input, tokens_output, p50/p90/p99 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, cache_hit_rate. Put these into a single CSV export per window.

4) Hyperscaler comparison: recommend we capture per-request cold-start latency and the time-to-first-byte metric (TTFB) to isolate network vs model init.

I can prepare a small script (k6 + OpenTelemetry stub) we can run from our lab to replicate your traffic patterns. If Evelyn confirms the infra contact we can set up a short SSH/allowlist window; we prefer an early-morning window PST to minimize interference.

Sergio
Director, Ops Product
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
